claim: LLMs cannot reliably self-correct reasoning without external feedback, and accuracy can drop after self-correction.
quote: their performance even degrades after self-correction
authors: Huang, Chen, Mishra, Zheng, Yu, Song, Zhou
title: Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
transfer: Any critic or pre-mortem step must be tied to a run, test or check; never a bare 'check your answer' call.

claim: A critical survey finds no prior work shows successful self-correction using feedback from prompted LLMs, except on tasks unusually suited to it; reliable external feedback is what works.
quote: no prior work demonstrates successful self-correction with feedback from prompted LLMs
title: When Can LLMs Actually Correct Their Own Mistakes? A Critical Survey of Self-Correction of LLMs
transfer: Gate revise rounds on an external signal (examples, tests, execution). Without one, skip revise.

claim: GPT-4 critiquing its own answers iteratively collapsed in accuracy on Game of 24, graph coloring and planning; a sound external verifier gave large gains.
title: On the Self-Verification Limitations of Large Language Models on Reasoning and Planning Tasks
transfer: Use a program-based verifier as the only judge of a candidate where one exists; a plain re-prompt with verifier output keeps most gains.

claim: Current multi-agent debate systems do not reliably beat self-consistency or ensembling at matched cost; results are sensitive to hyperparameters such as agreement level.
quote: current MAD systems don't reliably outperform methods like self-consistency
title: Should we be going MAD? A Look at Multi-Agent Debate Strategies for LLMs
transfer: Compare any argument or critic step against plain best-of-N at equal tokens. Treat agreement level as a tunable parameter. Quote is the fetch tool's summary wording, approximate.

claim: A single LLM with a strong prompt reaches nearly the same performance as the best multi-agent discussion method; discussion wins only when the prompt has no demonstrations.
quote: A single LLM with strong prompts reaches nearly the same performance as the best existing discussion approach
title: Rethinking the Bounds of LLM Reasoning: Are Multi-Agent Discussions the Key?
transfer: Do not build an argument step on the claim that debate beats one good prompt with examples. Quote wording approximate (from fetch summary).

claim: The original multi-agent debate paper reports gains on math, strategy and factuality; later critiques (c-04, c-05) suggest the gain may be mostly extra sampling.
quote: multiple language model instances propose and debate their individual responses
title: Improving Factuality and Reasoning in Language Models through Multiagent Debate
transfer: Treat debate as a costly sampler; adopt only if it beats matched best-of-N.

claim: Multi-agent LLM systems often give minimal gains on popular benchmarks; 1,600+ traces from 7 frameworks were annotated into 14 failure modes, including task verification failures.
quote: their performance gains on popular benchmarks are often minimal
title: Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?
transfer: Add an explicit program-based verification step; log failure modes of our own schema runs against this taxonomy.

claim: Chain-of-thought lowers accuracy on tasks where deliberation also hurts humans; one task dropped up to 36.3 points for o1-preview versus GPT-4o.
quote: up to 36.3\% absolute accuracy for OpenAI o1-preview compared to GPT-4o
authors: Liu, Geng, Wu, Sucholutsky, Lombrozo, Griffiths
title: Mind Your Step (by Step): Chain-of-Thought can Reduce Performance on Tasks where Thinking Makes Humans Worse
transfer: Router should skip deliberation on task types where human deliberation is known to hurt. Fits our puzzle losses.

claim: A meta-analysis of 100+ papers plus 20 datasets and 14 models finds chain-of-thought helps mainly on math and symbolic tasks, little elsewhere.
quote: CoT gives strong performance benefits primarily on tasks involving math or logic
authors: Sprague, Yin, Rodriguez, Jiang, Wadhwa, Singhal, Zhao, Ye, Mahowald, Durrett
title: To CoT or not to CoT? Chain-of-thought helps mainly on math and symbolic reasoning
transfer: Route: use extended reasoning only for math or symbolic items; answer directly otherwise.

claim: Chain-of-thought explanations can misrepresent the real reason for an answer, and biased context cut accuracy by up to 36% on BIG-Bench Hard; models rationalize wrong answers.
quote: CoT explanations can systematically misrepresent the true reason for a model's prediction
title: Language Models Don't Always Say What They Think: Unfaithful Explanations in Chain-of-Thought Prompting
transfer: A simulation or pre-mortem written by the model is not proof; require executed checks rather than prose rationales.

claim: LLM evaluators rate their own outputs higher than equal-quality outputs of others, and self-recognition causes self-preference.
quote: a linear correlation between self-recognition capability and the strength of self-preference bias
title: LLM Evaluators Recognize and Favor Their Own Generations
transfer: Strip authorship and shuffle candidates before any model judge; best to judge by execution.

claim: Einstellung in chess is bounded: it occurs when the familiar move is good but not best; when the familiar move is a blunder, experts and most novices avoid it and the effect largely disappears.
quote: the presence of a familiar solution can block the discovery of better solutions
title: The Mechanisms and Boundary Conditions of the Einstellung Effect in Chess: Evidence from Eye Movements
n: expert and novice players (n not read)
transfer: Run a 'seek a better rival' step only when the first answer passes checks but may be suboptimal; skip when it fails checks or is clearly right.

claim: Frontier LLMs reach high accuracy on medical cases but have severe bias trap rates when evidence is altered to change the correct diagnosis (Einstellung-like anchoring on statistical shortcuts).
quote: frontier models achieve high baseline accuracy but severe bias trap rates
title: MedEinst: Benchmarking the Einstellung Effect in Medical LLMs through Counterfactual Differential Diagnosis
transfer: On tasks with a possible trap variant, test the first answer against a counterfactual input that flips the answer. The earlier brief's 60.9% figure was not confirmed here.

claim: Larger GPT-3 models showed human-like intuitive errors, while ChatGPT models mostly avoided them, even when forced to answer briefly; CRT correct 96% for ChatGPT-4, 5% for davinci-003, 38% for humans.
quote: tend to respond correctly, avoiding the traps embedded in the tasks
title: Human-like intuitive behavior and reasoning biases emerged in large language models but disappeared in ChatGPT
transfer: Strong models may not need a slow override on trap questions; measure per model whether forced deliberation adds anything.

claim: Transformers handle multi-step compositional tasks by matching linearized subgraphs, and accuracy decays fast as task complexity grows.
quote: linearized subgraph matching, without necessarily developing systematic problem-solving skills
title: Faith and Fate: Limits of Transformers on Compositionality
transfer: Do not expect mental simulation of a deep line to be reliable; split long chains into short checked steps with code.

claim: The argumentative theory says reasoning aims at persuasion, so solitary reasoning is biased toward supporting existing views. It is a theory with a large commentary literature that I could not read.
quote: Skilled arguers, however, are not after the truth but after arguments supporting their views.
title: Why do humans reason? Arguments for an argumentative theory
transfer: Models have no persuasion stake; do not import social-debate benefits. Use another call's critique only when tied to a run.

claim: The premortem '30% more reasons' figure counts reasons generated, not their quality; I found no study showing premortems improve real decision outcomes.
quote: imagining an event has already happened raised the number of reasons people generated by about 30%
authors: Mitchell, Russo, Pennington (as summarized by a search result)
title: Back to the future: temporal perspective in the explanation of events
transfer: Use pre-mortem only before costly steps and measure avoided failures, not text volume. Quote is the search tool's summary wording, not the paper; original unread.

claim: A premortem study (Veinott et al. 2010, 178 students, H1N1 lockdown plan, per a secondary summary) found imagining failure lowered confidence in the plan more than pros/cons, but measured confidence, not plan outcomes.
quote: This measures confidence, not whether the plans worked out better.
authors: Veinott et al. (as summarized by a search result)
title: title not confirmed
transfer: A pre-mortem lowers confidence; in an agent it may add needless doubt, so gate it. Quote is the search tool's wording, unverified against the paper.
